From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@northcoast.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike on priv cluster - immediate help needed

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency and a steady rise in 5xxs from our private VPC cluster since ~07:45 PT. Our user-facing inference tail is spiking to 1.7s p95 (was ~350ms) and a handful of requests start returning decoder errors. This started right after a rolling deploy of our application (no model change on our side).

Quick notes:
- Region: us-west-2 VPC (private deployment)
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat
- Approx 8% of requests have 502/504 intermittently
- We've attached a short metrics export and the most recent error dump

Can you triage or direct to the right person? This is impacting customer-facing SLA (we have an upcoming product demo in 2 hours).

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Infrastructure Lead, NorthCoast AI
Attachments: error_dump_20261006.log (text/plain), tail_p95_chart.png (image/png)

On Tue, Oct 6, 2026 at 8:35 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the details and the attachments, this is on my radar. I'm looping in our on-call Private infra engineer (Laura) and runtime lead (Marcus) to triage immediately.

Daniel,

I see the logs — initial glance shows increased queue depth on the decoder worker pool and steady growth in tail KV cache evictions around 07:30. That pattern often correlates with a sudden burst of large-context requests or a change in batching behavior.

Immediate actions I'm starting now:
- Pull node-level GPU/CPU metrics for the private cluster (attached CSV will be expanded)
- Snapshot active queue lengths and current batch sizes
- Temporarily reduce max_batch_size on your route to see if p95 improves (we can roll back immediately)

If safe, could NC run a quick sample of recent request headers (content-length, seq_len) for ~07:20–07:40 so we can confirm request size shift?

I'll post updates here in the thread.

Laura Bennett
Senior Site Reliability Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@northcoast.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike on priv cluster - immediate help needed

Laura —

I pulled the runtime traces (INF-5723) and I can see the decoder stage has a backlog; some workers are spending more time in soft-float paths suggesting a model is hitting a different kernel (possible quantization fallback). That could be caused by a model file variant or a new inference request pattern triggering longer sequences.

Proposed mitigation steps we can run now (low-risk):
1) Force route to a compatible model variant (quantized variant already present) for 15 minutes to test latency impact
2) Apply temporary decode concurrency cap per node (reduce concurrency to favor latency over throughput)
3) Trim max_batch_size on the affected route to 8

I'll prepare a small patch for option (3) and push to your control-plane config if you sign off.

Marcus Lin
Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: node_metrics_20261006.csv
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@northcoast.ai>

Thanks Marcus/Laura —

We just verified there were two large batched inference bursts from a downstream analytics job around 07:25 that had longer contexts (mean seq_len ~1200). We did not change model binaries or quantization. We approve the temporary config changes — please proceed with the batch size trim and the concurrency cap.

Please also keep the canary variant ready; we'll need to run an A/B for 30 minutes.

Daniel
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Escalation summary & exec action (NorthCoast AI)

Team —

Thanks for the fast triage on this. Summary for leadership: NorthCoast AI experienced an immediate p95 increase due to unexpected large-context batches from a downstream job. Triage actions taken by the team:
- Reduced max_batch_size to 8 on the affected route (deployed 09:35 PT 10/06)
- Applied per-node concurrency cap to prioritize latency
- Prepared and validated a compatible quantized model variant for a controlled canary run

Impact: p95 returned to ~380–420ms within 20 minutes of the mitigation; 5xxs dropped to baseline. Customer demo later that day proceeded with degraded but acceptable latency.

Exec asks:
- Recommend a short SLA credit for the impacted window (proposal: 5% of October usage for the affected routes) — please approve with finance/legal if we proceed.
- Ask Product to evaluate an automatic safeguard that detects large-context burst patterns and auto-throttles batch size at the control-plane level.
- Engage Solutions Architecture to run a brief workload characterization for NC so we can recommend model routing + cache sizing changes.

@Rachel — please coordinate the customer follow-up and CC me on the final note. I'll start the finance approval thread for the proposed credit.

—Monica
